source: Minchat Shai on Gen 22:11 ('one of THREE doubled Names with paseq among them, as I will explain at משה משה in Exodus')
claim_en: אברהם אברהם ('Abraham, Abraham!' — the angel's sky-call that stops the knife) — the doubled call. Consonant-adjacency finds the name doubled at exactly TWO Torah sites: the call (22:11) and the toledot seam ('the son of Abraham; Abraham fathered Isaac,' 25:19 — a sentence-boundary doubling, not a call). The tradition's paseq-list (the vertical divider stroke between call-doublings) picks the calls: Abraham here, Jacob (46:2), Moses (Exod 3:4) — the stroke itself is uninstrumented (gap).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 22:11 (the three-list, second member)
claim_en: ...the second doubled call: יעקב יעקב ('Jacob, Jacob' — the night-visions at the descent to Egypt), one Torah site.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 22:11 (the three-list, third member)
claim_en: ...the third: משה משה (the bush-call, Exod 3:4), one Torah site — and all three doubled calls are answered with the same word: הנני ('here I am').

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 22:7 ('the nun of the self-speaking suffix DAGESHED, against custom; the Masorah: TWO such — הנני בני here and at מי אתה בני of Isaac's toledot')
claim_en: THE TWO FATHER-ANSWERS: הנני ('here I am, MY SON' — Abraham to Isaac carrying the wood) — the suffix nun DAGESHED against custom (both nuns dotted), the first nun in segol, no maqqef; the Masorah counts exactly TWO such tokens in the Torah, and the second is Isaac himself answering Jacob ('here I am; who are you, my son,' 27:18): the only two dageshed here-I-ams are a father answering 'my son' — on the way to the binding, and in the blessing-deception. SNAPSHOT census: 22 הנני tokens, exactly these two doubled.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 22:7 (the pair's second leg)
claim_en: ...the second father-answer verified: Isaac's dageshed הנני ('here I am') at the deception (27:18).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 22:7 (census frame for the pair)
claim_en: ...the census frame: the self-answer הנני stands 22 times in the Torah; the builder asserts exactly two carry the doubled nun (the pair above).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 22:17 (the Ramah: 'every inherit-verb in the Torah plene with two yods EXCEPT THIS — defective one yod')
claim_en: וירש ('and your seed shall INHERIT the gate of his enemies') — the Torah's ONE defective inherit-verb: written with a single yod where every other token of the form carries two. The Aqedah's inheritance-promise is the lean one.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 22:17 (the Ramah's rule, plene census leg 1)
claim_en: ...the plene twins verified: יירש with both yods stands twice — Sarah's exclusion ('the son of this maid shall NOT INHERIT with my son,' 21:10) and the locust-curse (Deut 28:42)...

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 22:17 (the Ramah's rule, plene census leg 2)
claim_en: ...and ויירש with both yods stands three times — Rebecca's gate-blessing (24:60, the verse that ECHOES this one) and the two Amorite conquests (Num 21:24, 21:32): five plene tokens around the one defective.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 22:17 ('the FIRST is the gate of his ENEMIES; the second — the gate of his HATERS, in Chayei Sarah'; the mnemonic verse named)
claim_en: THE GATE SPLITS BY ONE WORD: Abraham's seed inherits שער איביו ('the gate of his ENEMIES,' 22:17)...

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 22:17 (the second gate; Bereshit Rabbah 56's Tarmod reading via the Yefeh Toar note)
claim_en: ...while Rebecca's seed inherits שער שנאיו ('the gate of his HATERS,' 24:60) — the two gate-blessings, father's and bride's, differ by exactly one word; the mnemonic the Masorah hangs them on: 'upon your enemies and upon your haters who pursued you' (Deut 30:7).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 22:3 ('his two lads WITH HIM — and at Balaam, his lads with him: see there')
claim_en: THE TWO DAWN-SADDLERS: Abraham's נעריו אתו ('his lads WITH him,' the אתו with-word, 22:3)...

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 22:3 (the Balaam leg)
claim_en: ...against Balaam's נעריו עמו ('his lads with him' — the OTHER with-word עמו, Num 22:22): the two donkey-saddling dawn-risers distinguished by their with-words, exactly as the Masorah files them.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 22:5 (ונשובה SIX in the Masorah — 'in Abraham's merit Israel merited repentance... and if not: let us appoint a head and RETURN')
claim_en: ונשובה ('we will worship AND RETURN to you') — exactly TWICE in the Torah, and the pair is a moral scale: Abraham's worship-return from Moriah (22:5) against the spies' 'let us appoint a head AND RETURN to Egypt' (Num 14:4) — LETTER-IDENTICAL tokens (same pointing, same accent, builder-asserted): the same written word carries the ascent and the desertion. The Masorah's six-list adds the repentance verses (Hosea, Lamentations; edges) — 'all in Abraham's merit.'

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 22:10 (לשחוט two in the Masorah — 'we learn the offerings from Abraham: the daily lamb was bound like Isaac')
claim_en: לשחט ('to SLAUGHTER his son') — the slaughter-infinitive is UNIQUE in the Torah (one token, written defective); the Masorah's pair-leg is Ezekiel's altar-service ('to slaughter the burnt-offering upon them,' Ezek 40:39; edge) — the binding as the template of the offerings.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 22:17 (וכחול two in the Masorah — 'as the sand I shall multiply days': length of days promised too)
claim_en: וכחול ('and AS THE SAND on the sea-lip') — unique in the Torah; the Masorah's pair is Job's 'as the sand I shall multiply DAYS' (Job 29:18; edge): the seed-promise and the days-promise on one word.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 22:14 (בהר ה' three in Tanakh — Torah, Prophets, Writings — 'corresponding to the three pilgrim ascents')
claim_en: בהר יהוה ('on the MOUNT of YHWH it shall be seen') — the phrase stands ONCE in the Torah, here at Moriah's naming; the Kitzur's three-in-Tanakh legs: 'to come to the mount of YHWH' (Isa 30:29), 'who shall ascend the mount of YHWH' (Ps 24:3; edges) — one per division, as the three festival ascents.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 22:18 ('עקב אשר שמעת בקלי — the final letters: COVENANT')
claim_en: THE COVENANT IN THE FINALS: עקב אשר שמעת בקלי ('because you have LISTENED to My voice' — the Aqedah oath's closing four words) — the final letters run ב-ר-ת-י: the letters of ברית ('covenant'), as the Kitzur reads the seal of the verse.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 22:18 ('והתברכו — the resh with SHEVA, as our custom')
claim_en: DISCREPANCY: והתברכו ('and all nations shall BLESS THEMSELVES in your seed') — Minchat Shai rules the resh with plain sheva 'as our custom'; SNAPSHOT points HATAF PATACH (the compound half-vowel) — the bless-word vocalization split again (the מברכיך 'those who bless you' career-law class, run 4): the codex line writes the fuller vowel where the ruling wants the bare one. Filed to the watchlist.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 22:13 ('נאחז — the chet with PATACH in the early print and the precise manuscripts; Or Torah concurs; see Ibn Ezra')
claim_en: נאחז ('a ram CAUGHT in the thicket') — the chet pointed PATACH per the precise books. SNAPSHOT exact.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 22:13 ('בסבך — the second bet with PATACH too; one of the Masorah's FIVE adjacent same-letter patach pairs; Or Torah against the printer's emendation; Rav Paalim records a rival unique-with-qamatz Masorah')
claim_en: בסבך ('in the THICKET') — the second bet with PATACH likewise: the caught-ram phrase is one of the Masorah's five adjacent patach-pairs; SNAPSHOT stands with the precise books and Or Torah against both the printer and the rival qamatz-Masorah Rav Paalim found.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 22:16 ('ולא חשכת — WITHOUT maqqef')
claim_en: ולא חשכת ('and you did NOT WITHHOLD your son') — the not-word stands free of maqqef (the joining stroke), carrying its own accent, as ruled. Machine-checked by column.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 22:22 ('ואת בתואל — without maqqef, the aleph with TZERE, under tipcha; so in the precise books')
claim_en: THE LIST BREAKS AT BETHUEL: seven grandsons are counted to Nahor in one breath, six of them behind maqqef-joined ואת ('and') — and at the SEVENTH, בתואל ('Bethuel' — Rebecca's father, named two verses later), the ואת stands FREE: tzere-pointed, tipcha-accented, no stroke. The letter un-joins exactly at the bride's line. SNAPSHOT: tzere + tipcha verified...

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 22:22 (the maqqef leg)
claim_en: ...and the no-maqqef leg machine-checked by column.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 22:5 ('שבו — in some books without qadma'; 'לכם — under the lengthener, not tevir')
claim_en: שבו־לכם ('STAY here with the donkey') — SNAPSHOT realizes the no-qadma camp: the stay-word joined by maqqef, and לכם ('for yourselves') under mercha (the 'lengthener' accent Minchat Shai names), not tevir. Both machine-checked.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 22:5 (the accent leg)
claim_en: ...the mercha on לכם verified in the stream.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 22:4 ('מרחק written defective — read it מרחיק: the adversary kept DISTANCING the place before them')
claim_en: מרחק ('he saw the place FROM AFAR') — written defective (no yod, no vav), and the Kitzur rides the missing letter: read it as the DISTANCING — the place pushed away before them for three days. SNAPSHOT: lean, as required for the reading.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 22:6 (the Ramah: 'העלהו שם לעלה — defective; and EVERY burnt-offering word in the Torah likewise defective, save ONE plene; its sign: the olah of the first-fruits day, in Pinchas')
claim_en: העלה ('the wood of the BURNT-OFFERING') — defective, no vav, per the Ramah's whole-Torah rule...

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 22:6 (the Ramah's one-plene exception, censused whole)
claim_en: ...and the Ramah's ONE exception stands letter-exact on SNAPSHOT: the whole Torah writes the burnt-offering lean except a single plene עולה — Num 28:27, the first-fruits-day offering in Pinchas, precisely his sign-verse. The rule censused whole: one full offering in the Torah, and it is the festival of the new grain's.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 22:17 ('three seed-words in this passage — as Israel is called seed three times: of Abraham, of Isaac's sanctity, of Jacob's truth')
claim_en: THE THREE SEEDS OF THE OATH: זרעך ('your seed') stands exactly THREE times in the Aqedah oath (22:17 twice — the multiplying and the inheriting — and 22:18 the blessing), matching the Kitzur's three seed-callings of Israel (builder-asserted chapter census; no whole-Torah scope claimed).
